skill.name: bmad-orchestrator
skill.description: Coordinates BMAD project workflows, initializes configuration, tracks phase status, and submits phase documents to plannotator review gates.
skill.summary: Guides AI-assisted projects through BMAD phases with setup scripts, status tracking, and review gates.
skill.author: supercent-io

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown examples, shell helper boilerplate, or benign YAML parsing. Confirmed risks include remote curl-to-shell installation, cross-skill hook execution, unsafe Python fallback argument interpolation, and possible document disclosure through plannotator review.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-shell with a pinned package, checksum verification, and explicit user confirmation before execution.

remediation.issue: Installer executes a sibling plannotator hook script.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid cross-skill script execution, or require a verified absolute path and explicit user approval before running the hook.

remediation.issue: Python fallback interpolates shell arguments into python -c source.
remediation.suggestion: Pass DOC_FILE and TITLE through argv or environment variables, then call subprocess.run with fixed argument lists.

remediation.issue: Phase documents can be sent to plannotator without a separate privacy checkpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for confirmation before submission and document whether content leaves the local machine.

remediation.issue: Phase gate succeeds when plannotator is missing.
remediation.suggestion: Fail closed by default, or require an explicit recorded override before continuing without review.

content.value_statement: AI-assisted projects often lose phase context and skip review checkpoints. This skill initializes BMAD workflow files, shows current status, and routes teams through phase-based planning.
actual_capabilities: Initializes BMAD project config and workflow status files from templates.
Displays phase progress and recommends the next BMAD command.
Validates BMAD YAML configuration files and required fields.
Submits phase documents to plannotator for approval review.
Documents setup patterns for Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex, and OpenCode.
Supports project levels 0 through 4 with different required deliverables.
limitations: Requires local shell script execution for setup, status checks, and validation.
plannotator integration can send document content to an external review workflow.
Codex and OpenCode usage depends on external orchestration bridges.
It does not implement BMAD agents or generate phase documents by itself.

use_cases.title: Standardize feature planning
use_cases.description: Define a shared BMAD phase path before engineers and agents start implementation work.

use_cases.title: Resume a BMAD project
use_cases.description: Inspect workflow status and identify the next required planning or implementation step.

use_cases.title: Review phase deliverables
use_cases.description: Send PRDs, architecture notes, or sprint plans through a structured review gate.

prompt_templates.title: Initialize a Project
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Initialize BMAD in this repository for a web app named <project>. Ask me for any missing level or output folder choices.

prompt_templates.title: Check Current Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the BMAD workflow status and tell me the next required phase, blocked items, and the command I should run.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Phase Document
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the current PRD with the phase gate process, then summarize required changes before moving to architecture.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Cross-Tool Orchestration
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the BMAD phase plan for a level 3 integration project with Codex orchestration, plannotator review, and sprint handoff checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Check the workflow status for my level 2 project.
output_examples.output: The skill reports the project name, current phase, completed documents, required work, and recommended next BMAD command.

output_examples.input: Initialize BMAD for a new web application.
output_examples.output: The skill creates BMAD config, workflow status tracking, and a stories folder, then recommends product brief and PRD steps.

output_examples.input: Run a gate review for the architecture document.
output_examples.output: The skill prepares the document for plannotator review, records approval status when available, and explains whether to revise or continue.

best_practices: Review installer and network actions before running setup scripts.
Run workflow status before generating new BMAD artifacts.
Keep each phase document under version control before gate review.
anti_patterns: Running remote installers in unattended environments.
Skipping phase review because a tool is missing.
Editing workflow status manually without reconciling config and deliverables.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It coordinates BMAD workflow setup, status checks, phase routing, and review gates for AI-assisted software projects.

faq.question: Does it work with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes, but Codex usage is documented as an orchestration integration rather than the default native path.

faq.question: Does it create project documents?
faq.answer: No. It tracks workflow status and routes phases, but BMAD document generation happens through related commands or agents.

faq.question: Why does it use plannotator?
faq.answer: plannotator provides a visual review gate for PRDs, architecture notes, and other phase deliverables.

faq.question: Is shell access required?
faq.answer: Yes. The included setup, validation, status, and review helpers are shell scripts.

faq.question: What should teams review before installing?
faq.answer: Teams should review remote installer commands, plannotator data handling, and hook setup before running scripts.
